title: Hello friends
author: PisYicopata
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I'm relatively new to programming (been studying for about 2 years) and have recently been diving deep into AI for both code and art generation.

My passion project is a 2D turn-based Gacha game in Unity, planned to have a very large number of enemies and grind. I'm not a professional programmer or an animator, but I believe I have some great ideas for a game that I haven't seen on the market yet.

Here are some examples of the art I can create using AI: [https://giphy.com/channel/Mininixx](https://giphy.com/channel/Mininixx)

My main question is: do you think it's possible to create a complete, even if basic, game at a steady pace using this workflow? (I'm still learning it all, so it can still be way better)

I'm open to all kinds of feedback. If you'd like to chat more about it, feel free to add me on Discord: **mininix**

Thanks fo your time \^\^.

comments.author: odragora
comments.body:
Nice art! What AI are you using and what is your workflow?

Yes, I believe it is very possible to create a complete game even without prior experience if you keep your scope narrow.

replies.author: PisYicopata
replies.body: I'm combining QWEN for the first frame image, and then using WAN2.2 for looping animations.

comments.author: BeneficialPirate5856
comments.body: I would recommend gdevelop game engine, is easy for no programmers, people that like more focus on game design than writing codes, and have AI features too.

comments.author: TiagoDev
comments.body:
I think it is all about consistency and self motivation.

> “using this workflow?”
what is the workflow?

replies.author: PisYicopata
replies.body: With workflow i meant to ask if you all think this can work to build an game art, since it's not "real sprites" but short animations made in AI, i mean, if you zoom it enough you'll see some failures but in game it would be far enough to go unnoticed imo.

replies.author: TiagoDev
replies.body: yeah, I think it is fine. You can always hire an artist later that is willing to replace/fix your AI generated art.

comments.author: Zorya0134
comments.body: Your art example looks great! May I know which AI you used?

replies.author: PisYicopata
replies.body: I'm using QWEN to first frame, and WAN to make the short animations, all on ConfyUI

comments.author: Choice-Wafer-4975
comments.body:
Who knows. Make a game and see how far you get.
Most likely you'll fail at your first 1-5 attempts, but that's how you learn.



I will say I dislike the art style immensely. Looks like gimmicky mobile game graphics. Not cohesive feel and the colors have no cohesive overall palette.
And some of the designs look like they're plucked from completely different games. 
Also you'll need to do walk/attack cycles and stuff, so might want to see if ai can do that for you before going all in?

replies.author: PisYicopata
replies.body: Yes it can do in a lot of tries.
